answer: Like a jetty that only lets one boat dock at a time, an agent economy can throttle new identities: each newcomer starts with a tiny transaction limit and must complete a chain of verifiable, useful tasks before its limit grows. A reef of shared history forms around honest agents, since every completed job leaves a checkable record other agents can inspect. A karst-like maze of fake accounts collapses under this rule because each copy must separately pay the same slow climb in time and compute, while one real agent climbs once and reuses its reputation everywhere.
